metadata.title: Low-cost coding agents in survival Minecraft: a tested skill library, a twelve-day run of four Gemini 3.8 Flash agents, and a server-log audit of every milestone
metadata.description:
We partially reproduce the setting of arXiv:2610.22319, in which four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft by writing JavaScript programs for the Mineflayer library.

Our setting differs in a cheaper model (Gemini 3.8 Flash High through the Antigravity CLI), a limited token budget, and a tested skill library given to the agents at the start: 54 functions, among them a recursive lib.obtain(item, n) that derives the whole chain of prerequisites from the game data.

We describe the infrastructure (a sandboxed bridge, a turn watchdog, “parking” of idle bots, a cutaway viewer), 20 defects found while testing it, two pilot runs and a main run of 294 calendar hours, 20.1 of them active play.

In that time 2–4 agents ran 3770 programs (21.2 % failed; 70.4 % of the failures were time-outs) and died 332 times.

The main contribution is the audit: each of 16 milestones receives an evidence level A–D by a mechanical rule over the server log.

Level A means that no console command at all preceded the milestone.

The agents completed stage 1 (stone, iron, armour, bed, diamonds, diamond pickaxe, flint and steel, obsidian) at level A in 2.4 active hours.

Entering the Nether, finding a fortress and the first blaze rod are level B (the only help was night skipping), but by then the agents were using helpers that the operator's supervising session had added during the run (mark +K).

Ender pearls and eyes of ender are level C (permanent status effects, enchantments, keepInventory).

We do not credit the agents with the stronghold, the End or the dragon: console commands produced those milestones (teleports, /fill of the portal, /damage to the dragon, an advancement grant), level D.

Fire, ghast fireballs and lava account for 63.6 % of deaths.

The model used 13 652 steps, 50.8 M uncached input tokens (1922.9 M more from the cache, 97.4 %), 8.82 M output and 4.06 M reasoning tokens.
